_partNote: These classes are mostly recognizable machines, so each tile takes the characteristic hardware and no two silhouettes repeat: a bare wafer cell, a three-bladed turbine on a tower, a squat bladed water runner, a long curved trough collector, a single turbine blade on its root, a waisted cooling tower, and a house with a roof array. Wind and the cooling tower are the only tall structures and they share no shape; the runner and the blade are deliberately opposite proportions.

partPrompts.1: A single square solar cell lying flat and tilted on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a very thin square wafer with all four corners clipped off at a diagonal, a set of evenly spaced fine parallel lines across the face, and two wider straight ribbons crossing them at right angles. The clipped corners and the wafer thinness are the identifying geometry. One bare cell only: no frame, no glass, no grid of many cells, no roof, no machine.
partPrompts.2: A single horizontal-axis wind turbine standing upright, seen three-quarter: a slender tapered tower on a low round base, a compact nacelle box sitting on top, and three long thin blades on a small hub, each blade broad near the root and narrowing to a point. One machine and nothing else: no second turbine, no hills, no clouds, no ground detail.
partPrompts.3: A water turbine runner standing on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: a squat wheel made of a solid circular crown plate on top and a ring band below it, with about ten thick curved blades filling the gap between the two, and a small raised hub with a flange on the top face. Clearly wider than it is tall. Not a propeller with three or four slender blades, not a flat ring or annulus, no shaft, no housing.
partPrompts.4: A parabolic-trough collector standing on a plain surface, seen three-quarter along its length: one long deep curved reflector channel, U-shaped across its width and open at both ends, carried on a simple frame of struts, with a slim straight receiver tube running the full length above the channel on short arms. The long curved channel is the whole subject. Not a flat panel, not a round dish, no tower, no second collector.
partPrompts.5: A single gas-turbine blade standing upright on a plain surface, seen three-quarter: one twisted curved airfoil, tall and narrow, sitting on a chunky serrated fir-tree root block at its base. One part on its own. No wheel, no disc, no row of other blades, no engine or casing around it, no shaft.
partPrompts.6: A natural-draft cooling tower standing alone, seen three-quarter: one massive concrete shell with a hyperbolic waist, wide at the base, pinched in at mid-height and flaring slightly to an open rim at the top, carried on a ring of short angled struts at ground level. One structure only: no steam plume, no chimney beside it, no buildings, no landscape.
partPrompts.7: A small detached house seen three-quarter: a plain rectangular block with a simple pitched gable roof, and one flat rectangular array of panels lying against one roof slope, its edge standing slightly proud of the roof. The house is the object and the roof array is the identifying feature. No garden, no street, no fence, no people, no other buildings, no clouds.
